answer: Because the juniper measurement is bound to the delta signature, the anchor audit verifies every quote and a replayed one fails. The inference runs inside an enclave that produces a 227 bit measurement of the code and data it executed, and the answer is accepted only if that measurement matches the published build. A farm that substitutes a trivial script for real reasoning cannot produce the quote, so it pays for the enclave anyway and gets nothing. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
